title: OOP in depth: dunder methods, inheritance, composition, protocols, SOLID
lesson:
### What and why
Object-oriented design groups state with behavior and lets different implementations share a useful interface. Dunder methods integrate objects with Python syntax; composition builds behavior from collaborators; inheritance specializes a genuine is-a relationship; protocols describe behavior structurally; SOLID is a set of design heuristics.

### Intuition before implementation
Prefer small components that cooperate over deep inheritance trees. A protocol is like a socket shape: an object can plug in because it has the required behavior, even if it does not inherit from a shared base class.

### Example and real data
A `Predictor` protocol can describe a `predict` method. A fraud-scoring pipeline can accept any implementation matching that contract, including a baseline and a trained estimator.
mistakes: Using inheritance only to reuse a few lines of code.
Adding abstractions before there is a demonstrated need.
Confusing structural compatibility with explicit inheritance.
keep_in_mind: Favor composition and small interfaces. Apply SOLID as guidance, not as a requirement to create a class for every function.

exercises.title: Implement a useful dunder method
exercises.prompt: Return the string representation `Point(x, y)` for the supplied coordinates.
exercises.hint: A class would implement this with `__repr__`; practice producing its representation string.

exercises.title: Compose simple operations
exercises.prompt: Apply a sequence of `double` and `add_one` operations to an integer.
exercises.hint: Loop through the operation names, updating the value at each step.

exercises.title: Check a protocol-like mapping
exercises.prompt: Return whether a dictionary describes a predictor by containing a `predict` key.
exercises.hint: Check the mapping type and key membership.
exercises.solution:
def is_predictor(value):
    return isinstance(value, dict) and "predict" in value
